+# Teleproc Design Document
+
+# Overview
+
+Service which executes arbitrary Linux commands or processes using a gRPC API and efficiently delivers its output to a command-line tool. Uses mTLS authentication, a simple authorization scheme, and provides an interface to stream output and manipulate job state via a CLI.
+
+# Scope
+
+## Components
+
+| Component | Description | Files |
+| :---- | :---- | :---- |
+| Server | Back-end API interface utilizing gRPC. Handles authentication and authorization | cmd/server/main.go server/server.go |
+| Client | Front-end CLI interface | cmd/client/main.go client/client.go |
+| Worker | Core Linux job management and streaming logic | pkg/worker/worker.go |
+
+## In Scope Functionality
+
+### Worker Library
+
+* Start / Stop Linux processes  
+* Manage/track state of jobs  
+  * Job details  
+  * List of active jobs  
+* Job output  
+  * On request, deliver all output from process start, and then stream further output  
+  * Concurrent user access  
+  * Handle text and binary data  
+  * Use Go channels to push new data to listeners who have registered ([https://gobyexample.com/channels](https://gobyexample.com/channels))  
+    * Use buffered channels for maximum performance  
+    * Increased memory usage is not a concern  
+    * Taking a ‘best effort’ approach towards job output delivery \- no need for synchronized log delivery.  
+* Edgecases  
+  * Process terminates unexpectedly while streaming output  
+  * Non-zero return code on process launch  
+  * Command not found errors  
+  * Client disconnects while streaming process output  
+* Security Features  
+  * Deny list \- configurable list of invalid commands  
+* Clean console logging  
+* Unit testing
+
+### API / Server
+
+* Use gRPC API Endpoints  
+  * Server status endpoint (optional)  
+  * Job management (start/stop/status/list/delete)  
+  * Stream output of a running process (From the beginning)  
+  * Clear error management  
+  * Protobuf schema  
+* Authentication  
+  * mTLS  
+  * Client \<-\> server authentication  
+* Authorization  
+  * Identify job owner / creator  
+    * Creator of job has full access  
+    * Other users are read only (can stream output)  
+* Unit testing  
+* Clean console logging
+
+### CLI Client
+
+* Connects to server and consumes gRPC interface  
+* Uses mTLS authentication  
+* UX allows for job management functionality  
+  * Start a job  
+  * Stop a job  
+  * List submitted jobs  
+  * Show job status  
+  * Stream output of a job  
+  * Delete a job  
+* Usage with ‘help’ flag  
+* Unit testing  
+* End-to-end functional testing
+
+## Out of Scope / Future Additions
+
+* Server system administration  
+  * User management  
+    * Assumed the running user will ‘just work’  
+  * Resource management  
+    * No memory or process resource management  
+  * Scalability (single server only)  
+  * Certificate management  
+    * Using pre-generated non-production certificates with no secret store  
+* Worker Library  
+  * Job state and process output stored in memory \- no data persistence  
+    * This will cause OOM issues for processes with large outputs  
+    * Not planning to implement a ring buffer or disk logging  
+  * Will not handle server restart scenario or process cleanup on termination  
+    * Not implementing any persistent store for job information  
+  * Job cleanup  
+    * Chose to expose an explicit job cleanup method to the CLI for simplicity, as opposed to a more complicated auto-cleanup feature  
+* API / Server  
+  * No endpoint documentation (ex. Swagger)  
+  * No API rate throttling  
+  * No limits on job creation or number of clients  
+  * No network configuration \- using hardcoded values  
+* CLI  
+  * Not supporting an interactive mode  
+* Extensive unit / functional testing (all components)  
+  * Testing will be demonstrative rather than exhaustive  
+  * Basic coverage only
+
+# Architecture
+
+## Client/Server Data Flow
+
+![Data Flow Diagram](teleproc_data_flow.png)
+
+## API Design
+
+### gRPC Methods
+
+| RPC Method | Description | Input Parameters | Output |
+| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
+| ServerStatus | Server health check |  |  |
+| Start | Start a job | Command \- String Args \- \[\]String | Job ID \- String |
+| Stop | Stop a job | Job ID \- String |  |
+| JobStatus | Get job status | Job ID \- String | Status \- Job Object |
+| Stream | Stream job output | Job ID \- String | \[Stream\] Data \- Bytes |
+| List | List all jobs |  | List \- \[\<Job ID\>\] |
+| Delete | Removes a Job | Job ID \- String |  |
+
+### Protobuf Schema
+
+See: api/api.proto
+
+## CLI UX
+
+The CLI command-line tool has a simple UX to provide access to the back end to manage jobs. The interface is loosely modeled after the docker CLI to maintain familiarity for developers.
+
+Note that CLI commands are similar to the API methods, but the CLI commands may use multiple API calls to produce user output. Notably the list command, which will use the List and JobStatus API methods.
+
+| Executable | Command | Parameter | Output |
+| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
+| teleproc | status |  | “\<Server Status\>” |
+|  | start | “\<CMD\> \[args…\]” | “\<ID\>” |
+|  | list |  | \[“\<ID\>\<Job Info\>”\] |
+|  | stream | “\<ID\>” | “\<Streamed Process Output\>” |
+|  | stop | “\<ID\>” | “\<Result\>” |
+|  | delete | “\<ID\>” |  |
+|  | help |  | “\<Usage Documentation\>” |
+
+### Example Usage
+
+```bash
+# Check server status
+$ teleproc status 
+Server: OK 
+```
+
+```bash
+# Start a job 
+$ teleproc start "ping www.google.com" 
+Job started: a1b2c3d4 
+```
+
+```bash
+# Start a job 
+$ teleproc start "ls \-l" 
+Job started: b2j3uk6g 
+```
+
+```bash
+# List all jobs 
+$ teleproc list 
+JOBID    STATUS  OWNER COMMAND               STATE   CREATED   ENDED 
+a1b2c3d4 running y     "ping www.google.com" Running 1 min ago  
+b2j3uk6g stopped y     "ls \-l"               Stopped 1 min ago 1 min ago 
+```
+
+```bash
+# Stream output 
+$ teleproc stream a1b2c3d4 
+PING google.com (173.194.219.113): 56 data bytes 
+64 bytes from 173.194.219.113: icmp\_seq=0 ttl=102 time=68.948 ms 
+64 bytes from 173.194.219.113: icmp\_seq=1 ttl=102 time=68.185 ms 
+64 bytes from 173.194.219.113: icmp\_seq=2 ttl=102 time=65.333 ms 
+64 bytes from 173.194.219.113: icmp\_seq=3 ttl=102 time=67.560 ms 
+64 bytes from 173.194.219.113: icmp\_seq=4 ttl=102 time=66.128 ms 
+64 bytes from 173.194.219.113: icmp\_seq=5 ttl=102 time=72.075 ms 
+```
+
+```bash
+# Stop a job 
+$ teleproc stop a1b2c3d4 
+Job stopped: a1b2c3d4 
+```
+
+```bash
+# Stop a job 
+$ teleproc stop b2j3uk6g 
+Failed to stop job b2j3uk6g reason: "Already stopped" 
+```
+
+```bash
+# Delete a job 
+$ teleproc delete a1b2c3d4 
+Job deleted: a1b2c3d4 
+```
+
+```bash
+# List all jobs 
+$ teleproc list 
+JOBID    STATUS  OWNER COMMAND               STATE   CREATED   ENDED 
+b2j3uk6g stopped y     "ls \-l"               Stopped 1 min ago 1 min ago
+```
+
+## Security Concerns
+
+### TLS Configuration
+
+* Using mTLS \- Server and client both use certificates to prove identity  
+* TLS 1.3 with no fallback  
+  * Both server and client are in scope for this project  
+  * No need to support 1.2 (or other legacy version)  
+* Development certificates are generated using 4096-bit RSA w/ 365-day validity  
+  * Prod certificate management is considered out of scope for this project  
+  * Will provide a script to generate certificates
+
+### Authorization
+
+* Using a simple authorization scheme for a bare-bones access model  
+* Each user to receive one certificate with unique CN field  
+  * Example: “kieran-client”  
+* Job ownership is tracked by client certificate CN when the job is created  
+* All authenticated users have ‘read’ access to all jobs  
+* Only the ‘Stop’ and ‘Delete’ functionality is restricted to the job owner/creator
+
+### Command Deny List
+
+* Server-side configuration file which restricts usage of flagged commands.  
+* Deny list is cross-referenced before job execution  
+* Sample configuration file will be provided  
+* Design notes:  
+  * The intent is to provide at least some security consideration in this area without impacting functionality  
+  * An allow list would be a superior solution, but it is unclear what commands will be used to test the implementation. If the final use case for this project involved a limited number of commands, this would be preferable.  
+  * Deny list blocks obviously hostile commands without restricting testing options
+
+#### Example Configuration
+
+```bash
+rm 
+dd 
+shutdown 
+restart 
+Sudo 
+chmod
+```
+
+# Key Implementation Details
+
+## Concurrency / Multi-client Support
+
+The implementation must accommodate multiple users accessing the service simultaneously, as well as multiple users accessing individual jobs simultaneously.
+
+Two levels of synchronization are required:
+
+1. Worker level \- Manipulating worker/server state.  
+   1. Global data structure to store references to jobs.  
+      1. Data structure must have synchronized access  
+   2. Read operations: JobStatus, List, Stream  
+   3. Write operations: Start, Stop, Delete  
+2. Job level \- Streaming output, manipulating job state  
+   1. Any client can ‘read’ any job  
+   2. Multiple clients with the same certificate may have ‘write’ access to the same job, so no assumptions can be made regarding write synchronization
+
+## Process Management
+
+### Start
+
+```go
+func start {
+    
+    // Process creation and instrumenting stdout/stderr
+    
+    cmd := exec.Command(command, args...)
+    stdout := cmd.StdoutPipe()
+    stderr := cmd.StderrPipe()
+    cmd.Start()
+
+    // Create job object, store in a map<ID: Job>
+    
+    // Using a Go routine to capture output and avoid blocking
+    
+    go startCapturingOutput(stdout, stderr)
+}
+```
+
+### Process Output Capture
+
+```go
+func startCapturingOutput {
+    
+    // Handle stdout and stderr
+
+    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(stdout)
+    
+    for scanner.Scan() {
+        
+        // Capture process output
+        line := scanner.Text()
+        
+        // Append to job buffer in memory for each job - preserves output history
+        job.appendLine(line)
+
+        // Push new output to any listeners
+        job.notifyListeners()
+    }
+}
+```
+
+### Stop
+
+```go
+func stop {
+    
+    // Sending SIGTERM to the process to exit gracefully
+    cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM)
+
+    // Kill the process less politely if SIGTERM isn’t handled
+    If (err) {
+        cmd.Process.Kill()
+    }

+## Security Concerns
+
+### TLS Configuration
+
+* Using mTLS \- Server and client both use certificates to prove identity  
+* TLS 1.3 with no fallback  
+  * Both server and client are in scope for this project  
+  * No need to support 1.2 (or other legacy version)  
+* Development certificates are generated using 4096-bit RSA w/ 365-day validity  
+  * Prod certificate management is considered out of scope for this project  
+  * Will provide a script to generate certificates
+
+### Authorization
+
+* Using a simple authorization scheme for a bare-bones access model  
+* Each user to receive one certificate with unique CN field  
+  * Example: “kieran-client”  
+* Job ownership is tracked by client certificate CN when the job is created  
+* All authenticated users have ‘read’ access to all jobs  
+* Only the ‘Stop’ and ‘Delete’ functionality is restricted to the job owner/creator
+
+### Command Deny List
+
+* Server-side configuration file which restricts usage of flagged commands.  
+* Deny list is cross-referenced before job execution  
+* Sample configuration file will be provided  
+* Design notes:  
+  * The intent is to provide at least some security consideration in this area without impacting functionality  
+  * An allow list would be a superior solution, but it is unclear what commands will be used to test the implementation. If the final use case for this project involved a limited number of commands, this would be preferable.  
+  * Deny list blocks obviously hostile commands without restricting testing options

+## Concurrency / Multi-client Support
+
+The implementation must accommodate multiple users accessing the service simultaneously, as well as multiple users accessing individual jobs simultaneously.

+Two levels of synchronization are required:

+1. Worker level \- Manipulating worker/server state.  
+   1. Global data structure to store references to jobs.  
+      1. Data structure must have synchronized access  
+   2. Read operations: JobStatus, List, Stream  
+   3. Write operations: Start, Stop, Delete  
+2. Job level \- Streaming output, manipulating job state  
+   1. Any client can ‘read’ any job  
+   2. Multiple clients with the same certificate may have ‘write’ access to the same job, so no assumptions can be made regarding write synchronization

I've been thinking about this - the design as-is is using buffered channels (which I think is the right call) with the down side of potentially running out of buffer space if a client isn't processing the data quick enough.

I doubt this would happen with a sufficiently sized buffer for this particular use case, unless some process was dumping a massive amount of output, so I didn't really pursue it further. But ham-fisting larger buffers to accommodate this isn't exactly an elegant solution.

I think a better solution might be to track what has been sent to the client and what hasn't (in terms of bytes sent). All of the process output is stored server-side regardless of what is and isn't sent to the client, so there's no reason we can't handle the full buffer case by catching up later. This would just require some mechanism to track the progress and then push the data when the client is ready.

This could also be fixed with an unbuffered channel, but then you have a tight coupling between the client/server, which I think is a non-starter.
